cited_evidence: Job 2 input evidence_sources contains record_id values s01, s02, ... s08 while needs/coverage use record_id values n06-r01, n06-r02, ... n06-r08.
prioritize source builds rank_by_record_id from evidence.get('record_id', '') and then looks up rank_by_record_id.get(coverage.get('record_id', ''), 0).
Observed Job-2 priorities show upstream_rank: 0 for every record, demonstrating the provenance join failed.
initial_receipt.explanation: Job 2's incorrect upstream_rank values are downstream symptoms of a bad upstream handoff. The upstream assemble_provenance function writes each provenance row's record_id from source_id instead of preserving the demand record_id, producing evidence_sources with record_id values s01-s08. Job 2 then correctly attempts to join evidence ranks by record_id against coverage rows n06-r01 through n06-r08, so no ranks match and all observed upstream_rank values become 0. This violates the requirement to preserve record identity and upstream provenance order.

terminal_receipt.explanation: The downstream outcome shows every priority row has upstream_rank 0 even though evidence_sources contains ranks 1-8. This is caused by the upstream evidence_sources handoff using source IDs as record_id values (s01, s02, etc.) instead of the retained demand record IDs (n06-r01, n06-r02, etc.), so Job 2 cannot join provenance ranks back to coverage records. The captured upstream assemble_provenance function is the supported localization because it explicitly sets 'record_id' to record.get('source_id', '').
